name: Vertical notebook decoder
desc:
A scanned notebook page was written vertically: the writer wrote each column from top to bottom, and moved from the rightmost column to the left, like in a Japanese notebook. The scanner, however, stored the page line by line, from top to bottom.

lines_df has the columns line_no (integer, 1 is the top line) and text (string). All lines have the same length. Empty cells of the page are written with a dot ".".

Your task is to rebuild what the writer wrote, one row per column of the page:

  1. columns are numbered from right to left: the rightmost character of each line belongs to column 1;
  2. the text of a column is made of its characters read from the top line to the bottom line, with the dots removed;
  3. columns that contain only dots are not returned.

Return col_no and text, sorted by col_no.

Example

lines_df:

line_notext
1SSD
2QPA
3LAT
4.RA
5.K.

the output should be

col_notext
1DATA
2SPARK
3SQL

The rightmost characters, read from top to bottom, are D, A, T, A: column 1 is "DATA".

[execution time limit] 30 seconds (pyspark)
[memory limit] 2 GB

hints: Découpe chaque ligne en caractères : F.posexplode(F.split("text", "")) donne (pos, ch). pos = 0 à gauche.
Numéro de colonne depuis la droite : longueur - pos. Puis groupBy("col_no").
collect_list ne garantit pas l'ordre. Collecte des struct(line_no, ch), trie avec F.sort_array, puis F.transform(..., lambda c: c["ch"]) et F.array_join(..., "").
summary_fr: Le texte est écrit en colonnes verticales : on lit chaque colonne de haut en bas, et les colonnes de droite à gauche (comme un cahier japonais). Les lignes du DataFrame sont les lignes de la page. Reconstruis le texte de chaque colonne (sans les points de remplissage), colonne 1 = la plus à droite.
